technologies.name: Replicator
technologies.trek_description: A wall unit that produces meals, tools and spare parts on request from stored patterns. It needs no raw material loaded and finishes in seconds.

capabilities.name: Printing solid objects from a digital design
capabilities.note: Consumer 3D printers are sold widely. Output is mostly one material at a time and takes hours.

capabilities.name: Atomically precise assembly of arbitrary objects
capabilities.note: Mechanosynthesis has been demonstrated on a few atoms at a time in labs. Scaling it to everyday objects is unsolved.

capabilities.name: Creating matter from energy on demand
capabilities.note: Particle physics can make single particle pairs. There is no route to bulk matter.

technologies.closest_today: Desktop 3D printers make plastic parts from a file in hours. Nothing builds arbitrary matter on demand.

history.capability: Printing solid objects from a digital design

technologies.name: Universal translator
technologies.trek_description: A device that lets two speakers understand each other even when neither knows the other's language. It works with languages it has never met before.

capabilities.name: Written translation between major languages
capabilities.note: Free, built into browsers and phones, and good enough for the gist of most text.

capabilities.name: Live spoken translation
capabilities.note: Conversation modes on phones translate speech back and forth with a noticeable delay and occasional errors.

capabilities.name: Translating a language with no prior examples
capabilities.note: Machine translation needs large bodies of text. Projects such as whale-communication research are early and have not produced translations.

capabilities.name: Conveying meaning across completely alien minds
capabilities.note: No known method. It would need shared concepts that may not exist.

technologies.closest_today: Phones translate text and speech between major languages. Quality drops for rare languages and noisy rooms.

technologies.name: Tricorder
technologies.trek_description: A handheld scanner that reads the environment, a person's body or a strange object, and interprets the readings on the spot.

capabilities.name: Heart and vital-sign sensing
capabilities.note: Pocket ECG devices and smartwatches are sold to consumers and cleared by regulators in some countries.

capabilities.name: Handheld medical imaging
capabilities.note: Pocket ultrasound probes exist but are sold to clinicians, not to the general public.

capabilities.name: Automated diagnosis of many conditions
capabilities.note: A $10 million competition ended in 2017 with no team meeting every requirement. Reduced prizes went to the strongest entries.

capabilities.name: Environmental sensing (air quality, radiation)
capabilities.note: Consumer monitors exist, but each measures only a few things.

capabilities.name: One device that senses and interprets everything
capabilities.note: Nothing combines medical, chemical and structural analysis in one handheld unit.

technologies.closest_today: Single-purpose gadgets cover heart rhythm, air quality or ultrasound. No one device does it all.

technologies.name: PADD
technologies.trek_description: A thin handheld slate used for reports, orders and reading. Crew members pass them around and pick up where the last person left off.

capabilities.name: Touchscreen handheld computing
capabilities.note: Tablets are mainstream consumer products.

capabilities.name: Automatic sync of documents across devices
capabilities.note: Cloud storage keeps files current across phones, tablets and computers.

technologies.closest_today: Tablets do this today, and cloud sync makes the pick-up-where-you-left-off part ordinary.

technologies.name: Comm badge
technologies.trek_description: A small pin worn on the chest. A tap opens a voice channel to a person, a group or the ship itself, with no handset needed.

capabilities.name: Calling by tap or voice with no phone in hand
capabilities.note: Cellular smartwatches place calls from the wrist.

capabilities.name: Messaging with no cell coverage
capabilities.note: Some phones can text emergency services and contacts through satellites, outdoors with a clear sky.

capabilities.name: Radio contact with no network at all
capabilities.note: Licence-free handheld radios have worked for decades, over short distances.

capabilities.name: Chest-worn voice assistant badge
capabilities.note: One startup sold such a pin in 2024 and has since stopped selling it.

technologies.closest_today: Smartwatches and phones handle calls, and satellite messaging works without cell coverage. The badge form factor has not caught on.

technologies.name: Holodeck
technologies.trek_description: A room that builds lifelike scenes and characters you can walk through and touch, then clears them away when the program ends.

capabilities.name: Immersive headset visuals and audio
capabilities.note: Consumer VR headsets are sold in large numbers.

capabilities.name: Touch and force feedback
capabilities.note: Haptic gloves exist and are sold to businesses and researchers.

capabilities.name: AI-generated interactive worlds
capabilities.note: Research models can generate explorable 3D worlds as you move. The scenes stay consistent only for a short time.

capabilities.name: Solid objects shaped from light and force fields
capabilities.note: No known way to make intangible light behave like solid matter.

technologies.closest_today: VR headsets give convincing sight and sound. Touch, free walking and believable characters remain limited.

technologies.name: Warp drive
technologies.trek_description: A propulsion system that bends space around a ship so it can travel faster than light would allow in ordinary space.

capabilities.name: Theoretical warp-bubble spacetimes
capabilities.note: A 1994 paper showed that general relativity permits such a solution. Later work has reduced the energy estimates but needs exotic matter or unavailable scales.

capabilities.name: Lab demonstration of any warp effect
capabilities.note: No credible experiment has produced one.

capabilities.name: Faster-than-light travel
capabilities.note: No evidence it is possible.

technologies.closest_today: The mathematics of a warp bubble has been published. The energy it needs and the materials it needs are unavailable.

history.reason: Baseline assessment when the tracker launched.

technologies.name: Transporter
technologies.trek_description: A device that scans a person or object, dissolves it, and rebuilds it at a distant location in an instant.

capabilities.name: Teleporting the quantum state of a particle
capabilities.note: Lab demonstrations have worked over long distances, using a classical channel as well.

capabilities.name: Mapping every atom in a small sample
capabilities.note: Atom probe instruments reconstruct a sample atom by atom, but they destroy the sample as they go.

capabilities.name: Moving everyday objects instantly
capabilities.note: No method known.

capabilities.name: Moving a person
capabilities.note: It would require scanning and rebuilding roughly 10^28 atoms. No path exists.

technologies.closest_today: Physicists teleport the quantum state of single particles. That is information transfer, not moving matter.

technologies.name: Phaser
technologies.trek_description: A handheld energy weapon that fires an adjustable beam, from a harmless stun to a destructive blast.

capabilities.name: Short-range stun
capabilities.note: Conducted-energy devices are sold to civilians in many places. They use wires or contact, not a beam.

capabilities.name: Directed energy at range
capabilities.note: Military systems use microwaves or lasers against people and drones. They are vehicle-sized.

capabilities.name: Laser weapon systems
capabilities.note: Armed forces have fielded ship- and truck-mounted lasers.

capabilities.name: Handheld beam with selectable settings
capabilities.note: Power supplies and cooling make this impractical at handheld size.

technologies.closest_today: Stun devices and military directed-energy weapons exist as separate products. None is a single adjustable handheld.

technologies.name: Tractor beam
technologies.trek_description: A beam that grabs a distant object and pulls it in or holds it steady.

capabilities.name: Trapping and moving microscopic particles with light
capabilities.note: Optical tweezers are standard lab instruments, sold to laboratories.

capabilities.name: Levitating small objects with sound
capabilities.note: Acoustic levitation holds droplets and beads in the air in lab setups.

capabilities.name: Pushing orbital debris without contact
capabilities.note: Studies show a thruster beam could nudge a defunct satellite. No flight test has happened.

capabilities.name: Pulling a ship-sized object
capabilities.note: Light and sound can push but cannot pull at that scale.

technologies.closest_today: Lasers and sound waves can trap and move microscopic particles. Nothing pulls large objects across a distance.

technologies.name: Deflector shields
technologies.trek_description: An invisible energy barrier that absorbs or turns away incoming weapons fire and space debris.

capabilities.name: Stopping debris in space with sacrificial layers
capabilities.note: Spaced multi-layer shields protect spacecraft from small meteoroids.

capabilities.name: Intercepting incoming projectiles
capabilities.note: Vehicle protection systems detect and destroy incoming rounds. They are military hardware.

capabilities.name: An invisible force-field barrier
capabilities.note: No known physics lets a field stop matter and energy without a physical structure.

technologies.closest_today: Physical armour and active defence systems stop some projectiles. No invisible barrier exists.

history.capability: Stopping debris in space with sacrificial layers

technologies.name: Cloaking device
technologies.trek_description: A system that hides a ship from sight and sensors by bending or absorbing the signals that would reveal it.

capabilities.name: Hiding a small object from one band of light
capabilities.note: Lab cloaks work for specific wavelengths and viewing angles, and on small objects.

capabilities.name: Reducing radar visibility
capabilities.note: Stealth aircraft shrink their radar signature but remain visible to other sensors.

capabilities.name: Full-spectrum invisibility of a large object
capabilities.note: No method hides something from every sensor at once.

technologies.closest_today: Metamaterials have hidden small objects from narrow bands of microwave light. Stealth aircraft just reduce radar returns.

technologies.name: Hypospray
technologies.trek_description: A pressurised injector that pushes medicine through the skin without a needle, using doses the device chooses.

capabilities.name: Needle-free injection
capabilities.note: Jet injectors push liquid through skin with a high-pressure stream. Needle-free insulin injectors are sold in some markets, with a prescription. Most patients still use needles.

capabilities.name: Microneedle patches for painless delivery
capabilities.note: Researchers are developing patches that deliver vaccines, insulin and other drugs. Drug-delivery patches are still mostly experimental.

capabilities.name: A device that chooses the drug and dose itself
capabilities.note: Diagnosis and prescribing remain human decisions.

technologies.closest_today: Needle-free jet injectors work today. The self-selecting dose does not.

technologies.name: Dermal regenerator
technologies.trek_description: A handheld tool that heals wounds and regrows skin by passing over the injury.

capabilities.name: Sealing minor wounds quickly
capabilities.note: Liquid and spray bandages are sold over the counter.

capabilities.name: Printing skin directly onto a wound
capabilities.note: Labs can print layers of skin cells. Printing onto a patient's wound is experimental.

capabilities.name: Scar-free healing of deep wounds with a handheld device
capabilities.note: No technique heals deep tissue without scarring.

technologies.closest_today: Liquid bandages seal small cuts. Spray-on skin from the patient's own cells is used in burn units.

technologies.name: Ship computer voice interface
technologies.trek_description: A computer that anyone aboard can talk to in plain speech, asking questions or giving orders, and gets accurate answers.

capabilities.name: Spoken commands to control devices
capabilities.note: Smart speakers and phones do this in the home.

capabilities.name: Open-ended spoken conversation
capabilities.note: Chatbots offer voice modes that discuss almost any topic.

capabilities.name: Answers that are reliably correct
capabilities.note: Language models still produce confident errors. Reducing them is an active research area.

capabilities.name: Running a whole ship's systems without supervision
capabilities.note: No AI system is trusted with that responsibility.

technologies.closest_today: Voice assistants and chatbots handle commands and conversation. They still make mistakes with confidence.

technologies.name: Subspace communications
technologies.trek_description: A radio-like link that carries messages across light-years in little or no time.

capabilities.name: Global internet access by satellite
capabilities.note: Consumers can buy satellite internet service almost anywhere.

capabilities.name: Laser links across deep space
capabilities.note: A 2023 flight test sent laser data from about 31 million kilometres away.

capabilities.name: Quantum networks
capabilities.note: Labs link nodes with entangled photons. This helps security, not speed.

capabilities.name: Faster-than-light messaging
capabilities.note: Physics rules out sending information faster than light with entanglement.

technologies.closest_today: Satellites give global coverage, and lasers send data from deep space. Everything is limited by the speed of light.

technologies.name: Impulse engines
technologies.trek_description: The ship's everyday sub-light drive. It moves the ship around planets and between nearby points without warp.

capabilities.name: Efficient electric propulsion in space
capabilities.note: Ion thrusters power probes and satellites, with very low thrust.

capabilities.name: Fusion-powered propulsion
capabilities.note: Designs exist on paper. No fusion rocket has flown.

capabilities.name: Sub-light travel at a large fraction of light speed
capabilities.note: No engine could reach those speeds with the fuel we can carry.

technologies.closest_today: Ion thrusters are efficient but weak. Fast, high-thrust propulsion would need a new energy source.

technologies.name: Inertial dampeners
technologies.trek_description: A field that cancels the crushing force of acceleration, so the crew survives manoeuvres that would otherwise kill them.

capabilities.name: Cushioning occupants in a crash
capabilities.note: Airbags and crumple zones are standard in cars.

capabilities.name: Raising a pilot's tolerance to high acceleration
capabilities.note: Anti-g suits help fighter pilots, and are professional equipment.

capabilities.name: Cancelling acceleration for everyone aboard
capabilities.note: Inertia cannot be switched off.

technologies.closest_today: Seat belts, airbags and crumple zones spread out crash forces. Nothing cancels inertia itself.

technologies.name: Food synthesis
technologies.trek_description: A system that makes any meal from stored patterns, with the taste and texture of the real thing.

capabilities.name: Plant-based meat and dairy analogues
capabilities.note: Sold in supermarkets and restaurants.

capabilities.name: Cultivated (lab-grown) meat
capabilities.note: Regulators in a few countries have approved sales. Availability is still limited to some restaurants.

capabilities.name: Any dish assembled from basic molecules
capabilities.note: Real food is too complex to assemble molecule by molecule.

technologies.closest_today: Plant-based and fermentation-made foods are on shelves. Making a full meal from scratch molecules is not.

technologies.name: Androids
technologies.trek_description: A human-shaped machine with a flexible mind that can serve, learn and work alongside people.

capabilities.name: Walking and balancing humanoid body
capabilities.note: A compact humanoid is listed for sale from about $13,500. Buyers are mostly researchers and developers.

capabilities.name: General-purpose household work
capabilities.note: Several companies demonstrate chores with a human remotely helping. None is proven in homes.

capabilities.name: Realistic expressive faces
capabilities.note: Expressive robots are sold to businesses for exhibits and research.

capabilities.name: A self-aware artificial mind
capabilities.note: No evidence anyone knows how to build one.

technologies.closest_today: Humanoid robots walk and carry things. They do not yet perform general household work reliably.

technologies.name: Bio-beds
technologies.trek_description: A medical bed with built-in sensors that tracks a patient's vital signs and condition, with readouts overhead.

capabilities.name: Continuous vital-sign monitoring from the bed
capabilities.note: Consumer sleep sensors track heart rate and breathing under the mattress.

capabilities.name: Full-body scanning
capabilities.note: Private clinics offer whole-body MRI to consumers. It takes about an hour and its health value is debated.

capabilities.name: Automated reading of scans
capabilities.note: Regulators have cleared many AI tools that help clinicians read scans. They are professional products.

capabilities.name: Instant whole-body diagnosis
capabilities.note: No scan reveals every condition in seconds.

technologies.closest_today: Sleep trackers record heart and breathing, and hospitals monitor patients at the bedside. Whole-body scans take an hour.

technologies.name: VISOR
technologies.trek_description: A visor worn over the eyes that gives a blind person sight, including views beyond what normal eyes can see.

capabilities.name: Restoring some sight with an implant
capabilities.note: Visual prostheses exist in limited use, giving low-resolution vision.

capabilities.name: Seeing heat
capabilities.note: Thermal imagers are sold to consumers, including as phone attachments.

capabilities.name: Natural-quality vision from an implant
capabilities.note: Research continues on higher-resolution prostheses. None yet matches natural vision.

capabilities.name: Streaming any sensor straight into the brain
capabilities.note: Brain interfaces cannot yet carry rich sensory data.

technologies.closest_today: Retinal implants return crude shapes to some blind patients. Thermal cameras extend sight for anyone, as a separate gadget.

technologies.name: Holographic doctor
technologies.trek_description: A projected, lifelike medical assistant who can examine patients, advise on treatment and operate on them.

capabilities.name: Symptom checking and medical Q&A
capabilities.note: Symptom-checker apps are available to consumers. They are not a substitute for a doctor.

capabilities.name: Diagnostic conversations at expert level
capabilities.note: A research system performed at least as well as primary-care physicians in simulated text consultations. It is not a product.

capabilities.name: 3D-looking figures that appear to float
capabilities.note: Consumer light-field displays show 3D scenes without glasses.

capabilities.name: Operating on a patient autonomously
capabilities.note: Surgical robots are common in hospitals, but a surgeon controls them. Autonomous steps have appeared only in early studies and trials.

capabilities.name: A solid, projected body that can touch a patient
capabilities.note: Light cannot exert force on a person.

technologies.closest_today: Symptom-checking apps and chatbots give advice. Light-field displays make 3D-looking figures. Neither performs surgery.

technologies.name: Antimatter warp core
technologies.trek_description: The ship's power plant, in which matter and antimatter react in a controlled way to release enormous energy.

capabilities.name: Making antimatter
capabilities.note: A few facilities produce antiprotons in nanogram-scale yearly quantities.

capabilities.name: Storing antimatter for long periods
capabilities.note: Traps hold small numbers of particles for minutes to hours in labs.

capabilities.name: Antimatter rockets
capabilities.note: Concept studies exist. No engine has been built.

capabilities.name: Net-positive power from antimatter
capabilities.note: Making antimatter takes billions of times more energy than it releases.

technologies.closest_today: Particle accelerators make tiny amounts of antimatter at huge cost. There is no way to make it in useful quantities.

technologies.name: Cortical stimulator
technologies.trek_description: A device that stimulates parts of the brain to restore lost function or control movement.

capabilities.name: Restoring movement after spinal injury
capabilities.note: Spinal stimulation has helped people regain movement in trials and early clinical use.

capabilities.name: Brain–computer interfaces for speech and movement
capabilities.note: Implants have helped people with paralysis control computers and generate speech in studies.

capabilities.name: Non-invasive brain stimulation devices
capabilities.note: Consumer headsets apply mild current to the scalp. Evidence of benefit is mixed.

capabilities.name: Reading and writing complex thoughts
capabilities.note: Current interfaces decode narrow signals only.

technologies.closest_today: Brain and spinal stimulation treat movement disorders and paralysis in clinics. Reading or writing complex thoughts remains out of reach.
